correctness.rationale: For i=p^k d and j=p^l e with d,e prime to p, the normalizing factor gcd(d,e)lcm(d,e)/(de)=1 leaves coefficient p^min(k,l). Thus all positive-p-valuation basis products with each other vanish, and a valuation-zero factor acts by lcm on prime-to-p indices without changing the other valuation. The coordinate map multiplies correctly since indicators of d|r and e|r multiply to the indicator of lcm(d,e)|r; the same unit-triangular divisor matrix acts separately on each valuation, so inversion works even in characteristic p. Independently, the span of lengths not dividing m is an ideal (a nonzero basis product has index a multiple of each input); hence discarding those lengths gives a unital projection to R_m and proves the full-to-finite existence assertion. Also checked the stated, different retraction: truncation of positive valuations commutes with maximum and preserves positivity if a≥1; if a=0 all positive parts vanish on both sides. Prime-to-p gcd cutoff commutes with lcm by checking prime exponents. In a block, scalar α≠0 solves first for the scalar of X then its vector, uniquely; nonzero pure-vector A gives one scalar on the line Kv and q^a arbitrary vector choices; A=0 reaches only zero with q^(a+1) choices. Counting targets by first factor gives (q−1)q^a·q^(a+1)+(q^a−1)q+1, then independent multiplication over τ(u) blocks. At a=0 this gives (q−1)q+1 per field, as required. It applies to all finite extensions of F_p; it counts ordered inputs (A,B) for which a solution exists, not triples or the size of a global fiber. The frozen code was inspected, not executed: it works with the normalized multiplication, counts images without asserting each solution-fiber cardinality, and samples retraction identities in prime fields. The independent proof check, not this supplemental enumeration, validates the general cases.
residual_risks: Only finite cycle supports, no chains. Fiber counts are for X within R_m; full algebra fibers can be larger.

value.rationale: There is a concrete division problem beyond binary coefficients in the cited formal-sum framework. The result connects finite supports in the full algebra to a small finite ring, provides a coefficient-level criterion and determines how often division is possible, as well as how many cutoff solutions exist. The count is elementary after the block reduction, but the combination answers a motivated solvability and enumeration question for all odd fields, rather than selecting isolated cases or counting already enumerated configurations.
residual_risks: No optimal running-time bound for locating the cutoff divisors or solving when support indices are encoded in binary is established.
